text:
Montreal got its man. Dylan Larkin made his Canadiens debut this week after Kent Hughes sent Kirby Dach, prospect Michael Hage and draft capital to Detroit for him, ending a saga that hung over both teams for months. A Michigan kid who spent his whole career in Detroit now wears the bleu, blanc et rouge, and he arrives at a moment when the Canadiens need a lift.

They are winless in three, outscored 12-4, and the chances say that slide is partly real (46% of the expected goals). The injury list is the reason. Chris Kreider is out six to eight weeks with a lower-body injury and Josh Anderson is on IR too; the Kreider, Anderson and Alex Newhook line was not driving play, but Anderson's energy is missed. Mike Matheson is on long-term injury, and Kaiden Guhle left the Colorado game after a hit from Gabriel Landeskog.

The record flatters them. At 14-8-4 with 32 points, Montreal is 5.3 points above what its chances earned, carried by goaltending that has stopped about 10 more goals than expected. Juraj Slafkovsky has two points in his last 10 against 7.3 expected, a drought that should end. Lane Hutson remains the reason to watch, and his pair with Noah Dobson gets 58% of the expected goals.

Our simulations give the Canadiens a 54% playoff chance. What to watch: where Martin St. Louis slots Larkin, and whether it wakes up Slafkovsky.
headline: Larkin arrives to a crowded infirmary
